Definition: to gleam; figuratively, to enlighten (by caution)
BiblicalUsage: Zahar means to gleam, and figuratively to enlighten by warning. In Exodus 18:20 Moses is told to teach the people the ordinances and "shew them the way wherein they must walk." In 2 Kings 6:10 the king of Israel is warned by the man of God and "saved himself there, not once nor twice." In 2 Chronicles 19:10 the judges are told to warn their brethren, and Psalms 19:11 says of God's judgments, "Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's warnings are a form of light, not a threat. I hold that the king in 2 Kings 6:10 was saved because someone warned him, and that Psalms 19:11 is right: there is great reward in keeping God's word. My position is that zahar shows me a God who would rather warn me than punish me, and I should listen the first time.
